candidates.expectations: Underlying EBIT guidance of EUR1.2-1.3bn for FY26 has been public since the 22 September 2026 pre-close update and was reaffirmed with the 12 August Q3 release, so the FY26 number itself is largely known; the open question is the FY27 outlook given on the day. No fresh sell-side consensus or estimate-revision data could be obtained this session (no outbound page access), so the expectations picture is incomplete and confidence is capped at Low.
candidates.priced_in: Partly priced in. Price rose from EUR6.956 at first mention (2026-11-01) to EUR7.698 on 2026-11-10 (+10.7%), a +11% two-week advance that included a 2026-11-02 volume-expansion session (8.3m shares versus a roughly 3m preceding norm) and a fresh 20-session high. The known-guidance part of the event is therefore reflected; the FY27 outlook is not.
candidates.bull_case: Hotel/cruise pricing and winter booking momentum carry into FY27, the market gets a credible FY27 EBIT path on 9 December, and the stock continues the re-rating off the EUR6.57 20-session low.
candidates.bear_case: FY26 merely meets already-public guidance while the FY27 outlook is cut on airline cost, fuel or softer bookings; the November advance unwinds in a single earnings gap that no stop can protect against.
candidates.pre_mortem: Most likely overlooked failure: the 9 December report is a sell-the-news event precisely because the guidance was pre-released in September, so the only new information is the FY27 outlook and positioning into it is long. Second: this object has now been carried for three weekly cycles with no setup ever proposed, which is how sunk research effort turns into an eventual chase.
candidates.red_team_argument: Strongest rejection argument: after +10.7% from first mention and with price at the 20-session high, any entry here is a chase into a binary annual report, and the thesis contains no edge the market lacks because guidance is public. It survives as research rather than being removed only because the event date is dated and material, the instrument passes broker/liquidity gates, and the structure is measurable and orderly. It does not survive as a trade: the catalyst is 24 days out (outside the 21-day actionable horizon), no separate nearer verified trigger exists, and no defensible stop/target with >=1.5R can be built from a 3-session-stale price history. Action is wait_pullback, not entry.
